# Span structure

Memory is a Corsi-style span task: squares on a 2×2 or 3×3 board light up
in sequence and the child taps them back in the same order (forward) or in
reverse (backward). Each item is one direction, board and sequence length.

```{r mem-items}
mem_items <- items |>
  mutate(direction = factor(str_extract(item_uid, "forward|backward"), c("forward", "backward")),
         board = recode(str_extract(item_uid, "2grid|3grid"), `2grid` = "2×2", `3grid` = "3×3"),
         length = as.integer(str_extract(item_uid, "(?<=len)[0-9]+")))
span_fit <- lm(difficulty ~ length + board + direction, mem_items)
span_coef <- coef(span_fit)
span_ci <- confint(span_fit)
```

```{r mem-span, fig.height=4.5}
#| label: fig-mem-span
#| fig-cap: "Calibrated item difficulty by sequence length, board and direction."
mem_items |>
  ggplot(aes(x = length, y = difficulty, colour = board, linetype = direction)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`2×2` = "#4477AA", `3×3` = "#CC6677"), name = "Board") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:8) +
  labs(x = "Sequence length", y = "Item difficulty", linetype = "Direction")
```

Each added square makes an item `r f2(span_coef["length"])` harder on the
ability scale (95% CI `r f2(span_ci["length", 1])`–`r f2(span_ci["length", 2])`).
At matched length and direction, 3×3 items are `r f2(span_coef["board3×3"])`
harder than 2×2 items (CI `r f2(span_ci["board3×3", 1])`–`r f2(span_ci["board3×3", 2])`),
and backward items `r f2(span_coef["directionbackward"])` harder than forward
(CI `r f2(span_ci["directionbackward", 1])`–`r f2(span_ci["directionbackward", 2])`).

# Board size across datasets and waves

```{r mem-boards}
run_board <- trials |>
  mutate(board = recode(str_extract(item_uid, "2grid|3grid"), `2grid` = "2×2", `3grid` = "3×3")) |>
  filter(!is.na(board)) |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  summarise(mixed = n_distinct(board) > 1, board = names(which.max(table(board))),
            .groups = "drop")
board_pairs <- wave_runs |>
  filter(wave <= 2) |>
  inner_join(run_board, by = "run_id") |>
  group_by(dataset, user_id) |>
  filter(n() == 2) |>
  arrange(wave, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(path = paste(board[1], "to", board[2]), first_run = run_id[1],
            years = as.numeric(difftime(time_started[2], time_started[1], units = "days")) / 365.25,
            change = (score[2] - score[1]) / years, .groups = "drop")
board_change <- board_pairs |>
  group_by(path) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(change), se = sd(change) / sqrt(n),
            years = median(years),
            age = median(age_at_run(first_run)), .groups = "drop")
switch_diff <- with(board_change, {
  i <- path == "2×2 to 3×3"; j <- path == "3×3 to 3×3"
  if (any(i) && any(j)) c(d = mean[i] - mean[j], se = sqrt(se[i]^2 + se[j]^2)) else NULL
})
```

Children do one board within a run (`r sum(run_board$mixed)` of
`r fmt_n(nrow(run_board))` runs mix boards), and which board a dataset uses
has changed between waves (@fig-mem-boards). So no child links the two
boards within a run, and comparing scores across boards rests on the
calibration. Children who moved from one board to the other between their
first two waves give a check on it: if the boards were mis-linked, their
change would differ from that of children who stayed on one board
(@fig-mem-board-change).

```{r mem-boards-plot, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-mem-boards
#| fig-cap: "Share of runs on the 3×3 board, by dataset and wave (datasets with 50 or more runs)."
runs |>
  inner_join(run_board, by = "run_id") |>
  group_by(dataset, wave) |>
  summarise(share_3 = mean(board == "3×3"), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  by_ds() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(wave), y = dataset_label, fill = share_3)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(fmt_pct(share_3), "\n(", n, ")"), colour = share_3 > .5), size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Wave", y = NULL)
```

```{r mem-board-change, fig.height=3}
#| label: fig-mem-board-change
#| fig-cap: "Change in score per year between a child's first two waves, by the boards used in each wave (mean ± 95% CI; paths with 20 or more children)."
board_change |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean, y = path)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, lty = 3, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = mean - 1.96 * se, xmax = mean + 1.96 * se)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n = ", n)), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Change in score per year", y = NULL)
```

`r with(board_change, paste0(path, ": ", f2(mean), " per year (95% CI ", f2(mean - 1.96 * se), " to ", f2(mean + 1.96 * se), ", n = ", n, ", median age ", round(age, 1), " at the first wave)", collapse = "; "))`.
`r if (!is.null(switch_diff)) paste0("Children who switched from 2×2 to 3×3 gained ", f2(switch_diff["d"]), " per year more than those who stayed on 3×3 (95% CI ", f2(switch_diff["d"] - 1.96 * switch_diff["se"]), " to ", f2(switch_diff["d"] + 1.96 * switch_diff["se"]), "). ", if (abs(switch_diff["d"]) < 1.96 * switch_diff["se"]) "There is no clear step at the board change. " else "That is a step at the board change, though ", "The comparison is loose: the two groups come from different datasets and ages, so a difference could reflect either.") else ""`

# Open issues

`r below_chance_issue()`
- Scores on the two boards are linked only through the calibration
  (@fig-mem-board-change is the one empirical check). A design with some
  children doing both boards in one session would test the linking
  directly.
- How long the span staircase runs, and what the error budget measures, is
  studied in [memory length](../studies/2026-08_memory-length/memory_length.qmd).
